title: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey says India should 'reclaim' Noakhali, Sylhet and Chittagong
dek: The Godda MP blamed Nehru for their loss at Partition. Neither Dhaka nor the MEA had responded by Saturday evening; Tipra Motha's chief backed him.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
BJP MP Nishikant Dubey has said India should "reclaim" Noakhali, Sylhet and the port of Chittagong from Bangladesh along with Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, blaming Jawaharlal Nehru for their loss at Partition. The remarks, made in a news-agency interview on Friday, have been widely reported in Bangladesh, where Prime Minister Tarique Rahman told a state ceremony on Saturday that no one must again turn the country into "a subservient state": "Not Delhi, not Pindi, not anyone else."

Neither the Bangladesh government nor India's Ministry of External Affairs had commented on the remarks by Saturday evening, and the BJP had not said whether they reflect the party's view.

## What Dubey said

Mr Dubey, who represents Godda in Jharkhand, said in the interview: "The time has come not just to reclaim Pakistan-occupied Kashmir from Pakistan. It is also time to reclaim the territories that Nehru ji forcibly handed over, whether it is Noakhali, Chittagong Port or Sylhet." He argued that the loss of Chittagong cut India's north-east off from the sea and that this was why the region was seen as "backward", according to reports.

He said the three areas had been part of the domain of the Tripura kingdom, that the then Maharaja had objected to Nehru negotiating over them, and that Nehru gave them up because he wanted the Muslim League in the interim government formed in September 1946. He also criticised the conduct of the 1947 referendum in Sylhet. Reports differ on the name he gave for the king.

Pradyot Kishore Manikya Debbarma, the head of Tripura's former royal family and founder of the Tipra Motha party, backed the remarks in a post on X, saying the "Greater Tipraland" movement had often been maligned. He was quoted as saying that with sea access the north-east would "no longer be worried about the Chicken's Neck", the narrow Siliguri corridor in north Bengal that links the region to the rest of India.

## The historical record

Noakhali, Tippera (now Comilla) and Chittagong were districts of British Bengal, and Sylhet was a district of Assam; they were not part of the princely state of Tripura. The Tripura Maharajas did hold a large plains estate, Chakla Roshnabad, as zamindars under British rule, spread over parts of those districts. Sylhet voted to join East Bengal in a referendum in July 1947, except for most of the Karimganj subdivision, which stayed with India, and the Radcliffe boundary award of August 1947 placed Chittagong in East Pakistan. Tripura merged with India in October 1949. India and Bangladesh settled their land boundary in the 1974 Land Boundary Agreement, finally implemented in 2015 with an exchange of enclaves.

## Why it matters

Relations between India and Bangladesh have been strained since the fall of Sheikh Hasina's government in August 2024, and the two countries have five weeks left to agree on the future of the Ganges water-sharing treaty, which expires on 12 December. Chittagong is Bangladesh's main seaport, and Dhaka has offered it for transit cargo to and from India's north-east under a 2018 agreement. For West Bengal, which shares a 2,217 km border with Bangladesh, such rows can spill over into cross-border trade, border management and the treatment of Bengali-speaking migrants.

Mr Dubey has made similar demands before: in the Lok Sabha in July 2024 he called for Malda and Murshidabad in Bengal and the Santhal Pargana region of Jharkhand to be made Union Territories, citing illegal migration. The BJP said then that the remark was his personal view.

## What happens next

Bangladesh's foreign ministry holds regular briefings, and any formal response, or a statement from the BJP or the MEA, would be the first official word on the remarks.
